s0201.literal: When Hua Jiao raised troops upstream, an edict ordered Minister of Works Chunyu Liang to lead the mass of armies in advance to attack.
s0201.idiomatic: When Hua Jiao raised troops upstream, an edict ordered minister of works Chunyu Liang to lead the mass of armies against him.

s0202.literal: When the army reached Xiakou, Jiao's fleet was strong and none dared advance; Guangda was first to lead elite troops in a straight charge at the rebel army.
s0202.idiomatic: When the army reached Xiakou, Jiao's fleet was strong and none dared advance; Guangda was first to lead elite troops in a straight charge at the rebels.

s0203.literal: Once the warships engaged, Guangda shouted in anger, climbed the ship tower, and encouraged the soldiers; the wind was fierce and the ships turned—the tower shook, Guangda's foot slipped and he fell into the water; he was submerged a long while and was then rescued and escaped.
s0203.idiomatic: Once the warships engaged, Guangda shouted in anger, climbed the ship tower, and encouraged the soldiers. A fierce wind turned the ships and shook the tower; Guangda's foot slipped and he fell into the water. He was submerged a long while before he was rescued.

s0204.literal: When Jiao was pacified, Guangda was made Bearer of the Staff, Wise Martial General, Area Commander over Ba military affairs, and Inspector of Ba.
s0204.idiomatic: When Jiao was pacified, Guangda was made bearer of the staff, wise martial general, commander over Ba military affairs, and inspector of Ba.

s0205.literal: At the beginning of Taijian he followed Equaling-Excellencies Zhang Zhaoda into the gorge mouth and expanded and pacified the garrisons of An, Shu, and the rest.
s0205.idiomatic: At the beginning of Taijian he followed equaling-excellencies Zhang Zhaoda into the gorge mouth and expanded and pacified the garrisons of An, Shu, and the rest.

s0206.literal: At that time the Zhou clan was plotting the lands south of the Yangtze and built many ships in Shu, also transporting grain to Qingni; Guangda with Qian Daoji and others led troops in a masked strike and set fire and burned them.
s0206.idiomatic: The Zhou were then plotting south of the Yangtze and built many ships in Shu, also shipping grain to Qingni; Guangda with Qian Daoji and others raided them, set fire, and burned them.

s0207.literal: For merit his enfeoffment was increased with the former to two thousand households; he still returned to his original command.
s0207.idiomatic: For merit his fief was increased with the former to two thousand households, and he returned to his original command.

s0208.literal: Guangda's governance was simple and essential; he extended sincerity and entrusted subordinates—the officials and people found it convenient.
s0208.idiomatic: Guangda governed simply and sincerely, trusting his subordinates; officials and people found it easy.

s0209.literal: When his term ended, all went to court with memorials requesting him; an edict thereupon kept him two years more.
s0209.idiomatic: When his term ended, all went to court to request him; the court thereupon kept him two years more.

s0210.literal: In the fifth year the mass of armies marched north, recovering the old Huainan lands; Guangda met the Qi army at Great Xian and inflicted a great defeat, beheading their Fucheng King Zhang Yuanfan, Editorial footnote marker 12. captives and booty beyond counting.
s0210.idiomatic: In year 5 the armies marched north and recovered old Huainan. Guangda met Qi at Great Xian, routed them, and beheaded their Fucheng king Zhang Yuanfan [12]; captives and booty were beyond counting.

s0211.literal: Advancing, he captured North Xuzhou and was then made Area Commander over North Xuzhou military affairs and [North] Inspector of Xuzhou.
s0211.idiomatic: Advancing, he captured North Xuzhou and was then made commander over North Xuzhou military affairs and [north] inspector of Xuzhou.

s0212.literal: Editorial footnote marker 13. Soon he was additionally made Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and entered court as Right Guard General.
s0212.idiomatic: [13] Soon he was additionally made regular attendant of the scattered cavalry and entered court as right guard general.

s0213.literal: In the eighth year he went out as Inspector of North Yanzhou and was moved to Inspector of Jin.
s0213.idiomatic: In year 8 he went out as inspector of North Yanzhou and was moved to inspector of Jin.

s0214.literal: In the tenth year he was made Bearer of the Staff, Area Commander over He and Huo military affairs, promoted to Renwei General, and Inspector of He.
s0214.idiomatic: In year 10 he was made bearer of the staff, commander over He and Huo military affairs, promoted to renwei general, and inspector of He.

s0215.literal: In the eleventh year Zhou General Liang Shiyan led troops to besiege Shouyang; an edict sent Central Army Commander Fan Yi, Left Guard General Ren Zhong, and others in detachments toward Yangping and Qin commandery; Guangda led troops into the Huai as a pincer to strike them.
s0215.idiomatic: In year 11 Zhou general Liang Shiyan besieged Shouyang; the court sent central army commander Fan Yi, left guard general Ren Zhong, and others in detachments toward Yangping and Qin commandery while Guangda led troops into the Huai as a pincer.

s0216.literal: The Zhou army captured Yu and Huo provinces; South Yan, North Yan, Jin, and the rest each [withdrew] of themselves, Editorial footnote marker 14. the generals all without merit, utterly losing the Huainan lands; Guangda was therefore dismissed from office and returned to his marquisate as a marquis.
s0216.idiomatic: Zhou captured Yu and Huo; South Yan, North Yan, Jin, and the rest each [withdrew] on their own [14]; the generals won nothing and Huainan was wholly lost. Guangda was dismissed and returned to his marquisate.

s0217.literal: In the twelfth year, with Inspector of Yu Fan Yi he led troops on the northern expedition, Editorial footnote marker 15. and captured Guo Mo's city.
s0217.idiomatic: In year 12, with Yu inspector Fan Yi, he led a northern expedition [15] and captured Guo Mo's city.

s0218.literal: Soon he was made Bearer of the Staff, Pacify-West General, Area Commander over the military affairs of the ten provinces above Ying, Editorial footnote marker 16. led a naval force of forty thousand, and stationed at Jiangxia.
s0218.idiomatic: Soon he was made bearer of the staff, pacify-west general, commander over the military affairs of the ten provinces above Ying [16], led forty thousand naval troops, and stationed at Jiangxia.

s0219.literal: Zhou's Anzhou Area Commander Yuan Jing led troops to raid the lands outside the river, Editorial footnote marker 17. Guangda ordered a detached division to strike and drive him off.
s0219.idiomatic: Zhou's Anzhou area commander Yuan Jing raided lands outside the river [17]; Guangda sent a detached division that struck and drove him off.

s0220.literal: When Houzhu succeeded, Guangda entered court as Pacify-Left General.
s0220.idiomatic: When Houzhu succeeded, Guangda entered court as pacify-left general.

s0221.literal: Soon he was made Pacify-South General and Inspector of Southern Yuzhou.
s0221.idiomatic: Soon he was made pacify-south general and inspector of Southern Yuzhou.

s0222.literal: In the second year of Zhide he was made Secure-South General, summoned and appointed Palace Attendant, again made Pacify-Left General, and re-enfeoffed as Duke of Suiyue commandery with a fief as before.
s0222.idiomatic: In Zhide year 2 he was made secure-south general, summoned as palace attendant, again made pacify-left general, and re-enfeoffed as duke of Suiyue commandery with the same fief.

s0223.literal: Soon he was made Central Army Commander.
s0223.idiomatic: Soon he was made central army commander.

s0224.literal: When He Ruo Bi advanced on Bell Mountain, Guangda led troops and set his formation south of White Earth Mound, pennants and drums facing Bi's.
s0224.idiomatic: When He Ruo Bi advanced on Bell Mountain, Guangda led troops and set his formation south of White Earth Mound, pennants and drums facing Bi's.

s0225.literal: Guangda personally donned armor, hand holding the drum mallet, leading and encouraging the daring dead, braving blades and going forward; the Sui army fell back and fled; Guangda pursued north to their camp and killed and wounded very many—thus several times.
s0225.idiomatic: Guangda personally donned armor, drum mallet in hand, leading the daring dead forward through the blades. The Sui army fell back; Guangda pursued to their camp and killed and wounded very many—several times over.

s0226.literal: When Bi defeated the generals and pressed the victory to the palace city, burning the North Wing Gate, Guangda still directed the remaining troops in bitter fighting without cease, beheading and capturing several tens and hundreds of men.
s0226.idiomatic: When Bi defeated the generals and pressed the victory to the palace city, burning the North Wing Gate, Guangda still directed the remaining troops in bitter fighting and beheaded and captured several tens and hundreds.

s0227.literal: When evening came he then removed his armor, faced the palace and twice bowed, weeping bitterly, and said to the host: "I myself could not save the state—the guilt is deep.
s0227.idiomatic: At evening he removed his armor, faced the palace, bowed twice, and wept bitterly, telling the troops, "I could not save the state—the guilt is deep.

s0228.literal: " The soldiers all wept and sobbed; thereupon they submitted to capture.
s0228.idiomatic: " The soldiers all wept and sobbed; thereupon they submitted to capture.

s0229.literal: In Zhenming year 3 he entered Sui according to precedent.
s0229.idiomatic: In Zhenming year 3 (589) he entered Sui according to precedent.

s0230.literal: Guangda grieved that his native dynasty had fallen; he met illness and did not recover, and soon died from indignation, aged fifty-nine.
s0230.idiomatic: Guangda grieved his dynasty's fall, fell ill and did not recover, and soon died of indignation at fifty-nine.

s0231.literal: Secretariat Director Jiang Zong stroked the coffin and wept bitterly; he then ordered a brush to inscribe on the coffin head a poem, saying: "Though the yellow springs hold regret, the white day still leaves a name; I grieve that you died for righteousness moved by duty, not that you lived ungrateful to favor.
s0231.idiomatic: Secretariat director Jiang Zong stroked the coffin and wept bitterly, then had a poem brushed on the coffin head: "Though the yellow springs hold regret, the white day still leaves a name; I grieve that you died for moved righteousness, not that you lived ungrateful to favor.

s0232.literal: " Zong also composed Guangda's tomb inscription; its gist said: "Disaster flowed through the Huai and sea; peril lost metal walls and moats; the time was straitened and fortune exhausted; the age changed and Heaven perished.
s0232.idiomatic: " Zong also composed Guangda's tomb inscription, which in gist said, "Disaster flowed through Huai and sea; peril lost metal walls; the time was straitened and fortune exhausted; the age changed and Heaven perished.

s0233.literal: Claws and fangs turned from righteousness; armor and helm knew no worth; alone he raised loyal courage and led defense with method.
s0233.idiomatic: Claws and fangs turned from righteousness; armor knew no worth; alone he raised loyal courage and led defense with method.

s0234.literal: Sincerity pierced the bright sun; spirit roused the hard frost; cherishing favor he repaid gratitude—how could he forget when he stroked the affair?"
s0234.idiomatic: Sincerity pierced the bright sun; spirit roused hard frost; cherishing favor he repaid grace—how could he forget what he had undertaken?"

s0235.literal: Earlier, when Sui General Han Qinhu crossed the river, Guangda's eldest son Shizhen was at Xincai; he with his younger brother Shixiong and their following went over to Qinhu; [Qinhu] sent a messenger with a letter, Editorial footnote marker 18. to recruit Guangda; [Guangda] was then garrisoning troops at the capital, Editorial footnote marker 19. and himself impeached himself before the Court Tribunal requesting punishment.
s0235.idiomatic: Earlier, when Sui general Han Qinhu crossed the river, Guangda's eldest son Shizhen was at Xincai; he with his brother Shixiong and their following went over to Qinhu. [Qinhu] sent a letter [18] to recruit Guangda; [Guangda] was then garrisoning at the capital [19] and impeached himself before the court tribunal.

s0236.literal: Houzhu said to him: "Though Shizhen is on a different path as a middle grandee, you are a heavy minister of the state whom I rely on—how could I treat myself the same as among the suspected?"
s0236.idiomatic: Houzhu told him, "Though Shizhen has taken another path as a middle grandee, you are a heavy minister of the state whom I rely on—how could I lump you among the suspected?"

s0237.literal: He additionally bestowed gold, and that same day Guangda returned to camp.
s0237.idiomatic: He additionally bestowed gold, and that same day Guangda returned to camp.

s0238.literal: Guangda had a squad leader Yang Xiaobian who was then with Guangda in the army, fighting fiercely and breaking formations; his son also followed Xiaobian, wielding a blade and killing more than ten Sui soldiers; when strength was exhausted, father and son both died.
s0238.idiomatic: Guangda had a squad leader Yang Xiaobian then with him in the army, fighting fiercely through the formations; his son followed Xiaobian, blade in hand, and killed more than ten Sui soldiers; when strength was spent, father and son both died.

s0239.literal: The historiographer says: Xiao Mohe's spirit crowned the three armies; he was a good general of the time; though he had no strategy, he was still the mere-man courage of a generation;
s0239.idiomatic: The historiographer says: Xiao Mohe's spirit crowned the three armies; he was a good general of his time; though he had no strategy, he was still the raw courage of a generation;

s0240.literal: yet his tongue was slow and his heart firm—was he not of the respectful kind like Li Guang?
s0240.idiomatic: yet his tongue was slow and his heart firm—was he not of Li Guang's respectful kind?

s0241.literal: Ren Zhong, though brave, decisive, and strong in cutting through, yet in his heart harbored reversal; he deceived and beguiled his lord above and stumbled into his own evil—despicable!
s0241.idiomatic: Ren Zhong was brave and decisive, yet his heart harbored reversal; he deceived his lord and stumbled into his own evil—despicable!

s0242.literal: As for Lu Guangda, he wholly kept loyalty and guarded the Way, dying for righteousness and forgetting his person—he was probably also a good minister of the Chen age.
s0242.idiomatic: As for Lu Guangda, he wholly kept loyalty and guarded the Way, dying for righteousness and forgetting himself—probably also a good minister of Chen.

s0244.literal: [1] His uncle by marriage Cai Luyang was then at Nankang—the Hall edition verification says "aunt" in the Southern History reads "elder sister."
s0244.idiomatic: On "his uncle by marriage Cai Luyang was then at Nankang": the Hall edition notes that aunt in the Southern History reads elder sister.

s0245.literal: According to the Yuan Gui, 847 also reads "elder sister."
s0245.idiomatic: The Yuan Gui 847 also reads elder sister.

s0246.literal: [2] Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry—according to the Annals of the Later Lord it reads "General of Chariots and Cavalry"; see Collation Note 1 in the Annals of the Later Lord, Volume 6.
s0246.idiomatic: On "[2] grand general of chariots and cavalry": the Annals of Houzhu read general of chariots and cavalry; see Collation Note 1 in Volume 6 of Houzhu's annals.

s0249.literal: [jian] Commandery Duke—changed according to the Southern History.
s0249.idiomatic: [jian] commandery duke—emended per the Southern History.

s0250.literal: Comment: the Song of the Southern Dynasties established Suijian commandery; the Sui Treatise under Sihui county of Nanhai commandery has a small note, "formerly Suijian commandery."
s0250.idiomatic: Song of the Southern Dynasties established Suijian commandery; the Sui Treatise notes under Sihui in Nanhai, "formerly Suijian commandery."

s0251.literal: [4] Grand General of Agile Cavalry—according to the Annals of the Later Lord it reads "General of Agile Cavalry."
s0251.idiomatic: On "[4] grand general of agile cavalry": Houzhu's annals read general of agile cavalry.

s0254.literal: Bi advanced on Bell Mountain—He Ruo is a double surname; Bi's surname is He Ruo; here only the personal name should be cited; clearly "Ruo" was interpolated; it is now deleted.
s0254.idiomatic: On "Bi advanced on Bell Mountain": He Ruo is a compound surname and Bi's surname is He Ruo; only the personal name should stand; Ruo was clearly interpolated and is now deleted.

s0255.literal: [6] Following Jinxi Administrator Mei Bolong in attacking Jing's general Wang Guixian at Shouchun—according to the Biography of Hou Jing in the Book of Liang and the Comprehensive Mirror in the second and third years of Emperor Wu of Liang's Taiqing, all read "Wang Xian Gui."
s0255.idiomatic: On "[6] following Jinxi administrator Mei Bolong in attacking Jing's general Wang Guixian at Shouchun": the Biography of Hou Jing in the Book of Liang and the Comprehensive Mirror for Taiqing years 2–3 of Liang Wudi all read Wang Xian Gui.

s0256.literal: [7] Advancing on Qi and Qiao—"Qi" was originally wrong as "Zhan"; corrected according to the Northern Supervisory, Ji, and Hall editions.
s0256.idiomatic: On "[7] advancing on Qi and Qiao": Qi was originally wrong as Zhan and is corrected per the Northern Supervisory, Ji, and Hall editions.

s0257.literal: Comment: the Southern Supervisory edition reads "Qi" as "Shu"—wrong.
s0257.idiomatic: The Southern Supervisory edition reads Qi as Shu—an error.

s0260.literal: Commandery Duke—deleted according to the Southern History.
s0260.idiomatic: commandery duke—deleted per the Southern History.

s0261.literal: [9] An edict made Yi area commander of the northern expedition vanguard military affairs—according to the Annals of Emperor Xuan, Yi in that year was commander of all northern expedition military affairs; the Comprehensive Mirror agrees; the one who was commander of the northern expedition vanguard military affairs was Ren Zhong, not Fan Yi.
s0261.idiomatic: On "[9] an edict made Yi commander of the northern expedition vanguard military affairs": Emperor Xuan's annals have Yi that year as commander of all northern expedition military affairs; the Comprehensive Mirror agrees; northern expedition vanguard commander was Ren Zhong, not Fan Yi.

s0265.literal: Southern [An] Marquis Xiao Fangju was made Inspector of Xiangzhou—changed according to the Southern History.
s0265.idiomatic: Southern [An] marquis Xiao Fangju was made inspector of Xiangzhou—emended per the Southern History.

s0266.literal: Comment: the Biography of the Lamented Heir Apparent Fangju in the Book of Liang also reads "Nan'an."
s0266.idiomatic: The Biography of the Lamented Heir Apparent Fangju in the Book of Liang also reads Nan'an.

s0271.literal: first year—deleted according to the Southern History.
s0271.idiomatic: first year—deleted per the Southern History.

s0272.literal: Comment: the Yuan Gui, 380 reads "Young Emperor's Guangda first year."
s0272.idiomatic: The Yuan Gui 380 reads "Young Emperor's Guangda first year."

s0273.literal: [12] Beheading their Fucheng King Zhang Yuanfan—according to all editions and the Southern History, "king" reads "lord."
s0273.idiomatic: On "[12] beheading their Fucheng king Zhang Yuanfan": all editions and the Southern History read lord for king.

s0274.literal: According to the Treatise on Geography in the Book of Wei, Jin province had Fucheng commandery and Fucheng county; Xi province's Xiurong commandery had Fucheng county—all in present-day Shanxi.
s0274.idiomatic: The Treatise on Geography in the Book of Wei places Fucheng commandery and county in Jin province and another Fucheng in Xiurong of Xi—all in present Shanxi.

s0275.literal: Great Xian lies south of Hefei and north of Liyang; in the nearby commanderies and counties there is none named Fucheng; it is suspected that "king" is correct.
s0275.idiomatic: Great Xian lies south of Hefei and north of Liyang; nearby commanderies have no Fucheng; king is probably correct.

s0276.literal: In the late Northern Qi, kingly enfeoffments were very lavish; Zhang Baoluo in Qi times was enfeoffed as King of Fucheng commandery and had already died; Yuanfan may be a successor son who inherited the enfeoffment.
s0276.idiomatic: Late Northern Qi enfeoffed kings lavishly; Zhang Baoluo of Qi was enfeoffed king of Fucheng commandery and had died; Yuanfan may be a successor who inherited the title.

s0277.literal: [13] [North] Inspector of Xuzhou—supplied according to the Southern History.
s0277.idiomatic: On "[13] [north] inspector of Xuzhou": supplied per the Southern History.

s0278.literal: [14] South Yan, North Yan, Jin, and the rest each [withdrew] of themselves—supplied according to the Northern Supervisory, Ji, and Hall editions and the Southern History.
s0278.idiomatic: On "[14] South Yan, North Yan, Jin, and the rest each withdrew of themselves": supplied per the Northern Supervisory, Ji, and Hall editions and the Southern History.

s0279.literal: [15] In the twelfth year, with Inspector of Yu Fan Yi he led troops on the northern expedition—"Yu" in the Southern History reads "Southern Yu."
s0279.idiomatic: On "[15] in year 12 with Yu inspector Fan Yi on the northern expedition": Yu in the Southern History reads Southern Yu.

s0280.literal: According to the Biography of Fan Yi, at this time Yi was neither Inspector of Yu nor of Southern Yu.
s0280.idiomatic: Fan Yi's biography shows he was neither Yu nor Southern Yu inspector at this time.

s0281.literal: Zhang Senkai's collation note suspects "Fan Yi" is an error for "Fan Meng."
s0281.idiomatic: Zhang Senkai's collation suspects Fan Yi is an error for Fan Meng.

s0282.literal: Yet according to the Biography of Fan Meng, Meng as Inspector of Southern Yu was in Houzhu's fourth year of Zhide, which does not match this.
s0282.idiomatic: Yet Fan Meng's biography has him as Southern Yu inspector in Houzhu's Zhide year 4, which does not match.

s0283.literal: Some suspect "Fan Yi" is an error for "Ren Zhong," since Zhong in the twelfth year of Taijian was moved to Inspector of Southern Yu.
s0283.idiomatic: Some suspect Fan Yi should be Ren Zhong, made Southern Yu inspector in Taijian year 12.

s0284.literal: [16] Area Commander over the military affairs of the ten provinces above Ying—"ten provinces" in the Southern History reads "seven provinces."
s0284.idiomatic: On "[16] commander over the military affairs of the ten provinces above Ying": ten provinces in the Southern History reads seven provinces.

s0285.literal: [17] Zhou's Anzhou Area Commander Yuan Jing led troops to raid the lands outside the river—according to the Biography of Yuan Jing in the Book of Sui, it reads "Yuan Jingshan."
s0285.idiomatic: On "[17] Zhou's Anzhou area commander Yuan Jing raided lands outside the river": the Book of Sui biography reads Yuan Jingshan.

s0286.literal: [18] [Qinhu] sent a messenger with a letter—supplied according to the Northern Supervisory, Ji, and Hall editions and the Southern History.
s0286.idiomatic: On "[18] [Qinhu] sent a messenger with a letter": supplied per the Northern Supervisory, Ji, and Hall editions and the Southern History.

s0287.literal: [19] [Guangda] was then garrisoning troops at the capital—supplied according to the Northern Supervisory, Ji, and Hall editions and the Southern History.
s0287.idiomatic: On "[19] [Guangda] was then garrisoning at the capital": supplied per the Northern Supervisory, Ji, and Hall editions and the Southern History.
